A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EvoBrain. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and corresponding content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original seizure detection and prediction results, runtime measurements, graph visualizations and ablations, including Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, a GNN-component ablation and GPU-memory measurements in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains correlation-based dynamic graphs, frequency-domain inputs, two-stream Mamba, GCN with Laplacian positional encoding, and max pooling. Appendix E retains the architecture and training objective. GIN and no-GNN variants are new ablations, not revisions to EvoBrain.

E1.justification: Both versions use TUSZ for seizure detection and prediction and CHB-MIT for detection and efficiency evaluations. No dataset, population, task or distinct input scenario is added; the new component and memory analyses extend evaluation within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the main comparison from eight to eleven baselines by adding SVM, Random Forest and EEGPT for both tasks and both window lengths. This broadens the comparison to conventional classifiers and another pretrained EEG foundation model while retaining every previous baseline.

E3.justification: The new memory experiment measures training and inference GPU memory at batch size 1, and the revised ablation introduces GIN and no-GNN controls. Existing splits, sample counts, metrics, windows and training settings remain unchanged. The one-minute preictal definition and five-minute exclusion buffer move from Appendix F to Section 5.1.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 5 replaces the pooling-method comparison from v1 Figure 8 with a GCN/GIN/no-GNN ablation testing the spatial component's contribution. The architecture, input-feature and Mamba/GRU ablations are retained and relocated. Appendix G additionally examines memory consumption alongside computational speed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify averaging over five runs with different random seeds and use the same uncertainty-reporting convention in Table 1. There are no new run-count disclosures, confidence intervals or significance tests. The corrected DCRNN uncertainty value is a concrete-result change.

E6.justification: The reported evidence expands through three new baseline rows, GNN-component AUCs of 0.88/0.87/0.85 for GCN/GIN/no GNN, and Table 4 memory measurements, including EvoBrain's 51.35/46.64 MB for training/inference. Pooling-ablation results are removed. Existing Table 1 means remain unchanged; DCRNN's 60-second prediction F1 changes from 0.397 ±0.29 to 0.397 ±0.029.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, expressivity theorems and lemmas, appendix proofs and counterexample, and Appendix D complexity derivations are unchanged. Differences are grammatical, typographical or due to figure relocation and renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same method, expressivity, performance, efficiency and early-prediction claims. The rewritten conclusion consolidates these existing contributions and previously discussed clinical potential without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving weak, diffuse preictal patterns and LaBraM's scale and pretraining, plus limitations concerning other tasks, demographic bias and false-alarm harms. Appendix G discusses memory-speed tradeoffs. The pooling-based interpretation about emphasizing localized seizure activity in v1 Appendix H is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix E replaces the anonymous repository reference with a named GitHub repository. v2 also identifies EEGPT checkpoint fine-tuning, reports its 51,221,121 trainable parameters, and specifies batch size 1 for memory measurements. Existing EvoBrain implementation details remain unchanged; repository availability is not independently established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Chen et al. (2025), Kotoge et al. (2024; SplitSee) and Wang et al. (2024; EEGPT), and removes Zheng et al. (2024; CI-GNN). The central positioning relative to static-graph methods and Gao and Ribeiro's dynamic-GNN taxonomy remains unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized grammar, title and author-contact edits, a rewritten conclusion, and new limitations and acknowledgments text. Prediction-task details and the revised ablation discussion move into Section 5. The overall narrative and method/theory organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains three rows, Table 2 gains an EEGPT column, and Table 4 is added. The appendix ablation figure becomes main-text Figure 5 with reordered panels and a replacement GNN panel. Clinical and theoretical figures are relocated or renumbered; existing ROC, dynamic-graph, runtime and clinical visualizations retain their content.

improvement.justification: The additional baselines, GNN ablation and memory measurements broaden empirical support, while Section 6 more explicitly discusses prediction and clinical limitations. These benefits outweigh the loss of pooling-ablation evidence, although implementation details for the added baselines remain sparse. The revision improves evaluation completeness and qualification of the findings without resolving a major deficiency in the core method or theory.
